# Experience Mod Analyzer

> A free browser-based calculator that recalculates a workers compensation
> experience modification rate (EMR) from an NCCI experience rating worksheet,
> verifies the worksheet against its own arithmetic, prices each claim's effect
> on the mod, and exports a PDF report. Published by CertifyMe.net.

The worksheet PDF is parsed locally in the browser using its text layer. It is
never uploaded and nothing is stored; refreshing the page clears everything.

## What it calculates

- The experience modification factor, recomputed from the NCCI formula and
  compared against the factor printed on the worksheet.
- The loss-free minimum: the lowest mod the experience period could produce
  with no losses at all. A hard floor set by payroll, classification and
  expected losses, not by claims.
- Each claim's contribution, in mod points and in estimated premium.
- Reserve-reduction scenarios for open claims, capped at the split point.
- Deterministic checks of the worksheet's internal arithmetic: payroll divided
  by 100 times the expected loss rate equals expected losses; expected losses
  times the D-ratio equals expected primary; excess equals incurred less
  primary; and the mod equals its own numerator over its denominator.

## The formula

Mod = (actual primary + stabilizing value + W x actual excess)
    / (expected primary + stabilizing value + W x expected excess)

where the stabilizing value is expected excess x (1 - W) + ballast, and W is
the weighting factor printed as (A) on the worksheet. The denominator reduces
to expected losses plus ballast, so each claim's effect on the mod is
proportional to its primary losses plus its weighted excess losses.

## Key facts

- A mod of 1.00 is average. Below 1.00 is a credit; above 1.00 is a debit.
- The experience period is normally three policy years: those that began
  21 to 57 months before the rating effective date, so the policy in force
  today is never included. A claim first counts about two years after its
  policy began and stays in for three annual ratings.
- The split point divides each claim into primary and excess losses. It varies
  by state and over time, and appears as its own column on worksheets from 2025.
- Excess losses enter the calculation only at the weighting factor, so primary
  dollars move the mod far more than excess dollars.
- In states applying the Experience Rating Adjustment, medical-only claims
  (injury type 06) have a share of their loss dollars removed, commonly 70%.
- A claim flagged as a limited loss enters the rating at less than its printed
  incurred value.

## Pages

- [Experience Mod Analyzer](https://emod-tool-2-0.vercel.app/): the tool, how
  it works, FAQ, and a glossary of worksheet terms.
- [What Is an Experience Modification Rate (EMR)?](https://emod-tool-2-0.vercel.app/what-is-experience-modification-rate-emr):
  what the mod means, the NCCI formula step by step with worked examples from
  NCCI's own sample worksheet, why claim frequency moves a mod more than
  severity, the loss-free floor, the 2024 state-specific split points, and
  which states NCCI's plan does not cover.
- [How to Read an Experience Mod Worksheet](https://emod-tool-2-0.vercel.app/how-to-read-experience-mod-worksheet):
  each field on the NCCI worksheet, the arithmetic that can be checked by
  hand, why the summary shows two loss totals, how much an error costs
  depending on where it sits, common errors and the dispute process.
- [EMR in Construction](https://emod-tool-2-0.vercel.app/emr-in-construction):
  what owners ask for on real prequalification forms, the Texas, Virginia and
  Indiana laws and the NCOIL model act restricting EMR bid cutoffs, how many
  small claims it takes to cross 1.0, and EMR compared with TRIR.

## Publisher

- [CertifyMe.net](https://www.certifyme.net): online forklift operator training and certification for employers.
- [Compliance Hub](https://compliance-hub.cloud): employee document and certification tracking for small employers.
- [CertifyMeOnline.net](https://www.certifymeonline.net): online aerial and scissor lift operator training.

## Notes

Not affiliated with or endorsed by NCCI. Not legal, actuarial or insurance
advice. The tool reads one document and cannot see claim files, reserving
rationale or payroll records, so its observations are points to verify.
